input.rationale: Follow-up on the registered necessary gap for the leader side of @q-snapshot-boundary. A new, independently assessable question targets the replication responsibility (leader nextIndex/SEND_SNAP) rather than the follower's ingest responsibility: given a follower that cannot be repaired at the snapshot boundary, does the leader re-ship the snapshot indefinitely with no progress on that follower? A live two-node harness (leader plus peer, one process, InmemTransport) was built and exercised locally as construction feedback: the control peer converged after a single InstallSnapshot, while the otherwise identical peer holding an earlier-term entry at the snapshot index produced ~15,900 InstallSnapshot calls inside a 1.2 s interval and stayed applied at the snapshot index. The experiment is registered so the controller can retain the receipt before any measured conclusion is asserted.

investigations.question: With a leader whose retained log begins above its snapshot index L and a follower that keeps advertising an earlier term for L, does one execution show repeated InstallSnapshot attempts and persistent non-progress on that follower, or does the leader converge after one snapshot?
investigations.hypothesis: The follower rejects every AppendEntries whose PrevLogEntry is L (stale term from getLastEntry). The leader computes nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1) = L, then setPreviousLog(L) needs the leader's own entry L-1; because the leader compacted up to its snapshot index, GetLog(L-1) returns ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, sendLatestSnapshot restores nextIndex = L+1, and the next append is rejected again. The cycle restores its own precondition and has no enabled repair, so the leader re-ships the snapshot repeatedly while the follower's applied index stays at L.
investigations.discriminator: Control peer and defect peer share one harness and differ only in whether an earlier-term entry occupies index L: one snapshot and applied index L+1 refute the suspicion; repeated InstallSnapshot calls together with an applied index pinned at L support it.

knowledge.statement: On a rejected AppendEntries the leader rewinds the follower's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1); when that lands on the follower's snapshot boundary L and the leader's own log has been compacted so that L-1 is no longer stored, the rebuild of the request returns ErrLogNotFound, which replicateTo maps to SEND_SNAP. sendLatestSnapshot then ships the current snapshot and, on success, sets nextIndex = meta.Index+1 = L+1, so the following append again carries PrevLogEntry=L. Nothing in the loop removes the follower's stale entry at L or advances the leader's nextIndex past L, so the state that caused the rejection is restored each round.
knowledge.conditions: Applies when the leader's log compaction leaves its first retained index at or above L (for example TrailingLogs=0, or a snapshot taken with more than TrailingLogs entries behind it) and the follower answers PrevLogEntry=L with Success=false because its view of L is a stale earlier-term entry rather than the snapshot's.

interpretations.rationale: Source identifies the exact cycle, but the measured end-to-end result is deliberately left unresolved until the controller retains an execution of this experiment. Local construction feedback on the same harness design showed install_snapshot_calls_early=1/late=1 with follower_applied_index=9 for the control peer, versus install_snapshot_calls_early=2675/late=15920 with follower_applied_index=8 pinned at the snapshot index for the peer holding an earlier-term entry at that index; that local run is not a retained receipt and is recorded here only as construction feedback. The cycle's weakest necessary link is the leader-side ErrLogNotFound branch, which depends on the log store reporting ErrLogNotFound for L-1 after compaction; the harness uses InmemStore, whose DeleteRange resets to empty once everything is deleted, and the leader's first retained index in that run was 9 with the snapshot at 8.
counterevidence: The control peer converged in one snapshot, so the repeated-snapshot behaviour is not a property of adding a voter alone.
In the same run the leader's own commit index still advanced to 9, so the no-progress claim is scoped to that follower's replication and applied index, not to the leader's commit index.
limitations: Source-only conclusion: the receipt for this experiment has not been produced yet.
Only InmemTransport/InmemStore were used; a monotonic LogStore clears all logs on snapshot install, which changes the store-level path but not the follower's stale last-entry term.
The peer's earlier-term entry was seeded by a legal AppendEntries from a term-1 producer rather than by a complete replica-set history; that reachability question stays open.

scope.description: One process, two real Raft instances over InmemTransport. server-A is bootstrapped as a single-voter cluster, becomes leader, applies six commands, then takes a user snapshot with TrailingLogs=0 so its retained log starts above the snapshot index. server-B is bootstrapped as a Nonvoter under the same configuration so it never campaigns, and is seeded with earlier-term (term 1) commands up to the snapshot index (defect) or one index short of it (control) via a legal AppendEntries from a third in-memory transport. server-A and server-B are then connected and server-A is asked to AddVoter(server-B).
assumptions: The isolated target runs the root package '.' directly, so the harness is an in-package test and may wrap the transport to count InstallSnapshot calls.
A single-voter cluster bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster reaches leadership on its own after the election timeout, which keeps the leader-side prefix free of partition machinery.
AddVoter is issued without waiting on its future because the config entry cannot commit while the peer is unrepairable; the observation window starts after a fixed delay.
excluded: No network transport, no partitions, and no more than one peer; leader elections among multiple voters are out of scope.
The follower-side boundary rejection is already covered by the earlier experiment and is not re-derived here.

experiment.prefix: server-A: inmem transport wrapped by a counting decorator that increments on every InstallSnapshot call; BootstrapCluster(conf.TrailingLogs=0, config={A:Voter}); NewRaft; wait for Leader; six Apply(new command) calls; Snapshot() and record its Index L and the store's FirstIndex. server-B: separate inmem transport, BootstrapCluster(config={A:Voter,B:Nonvoter}) then NewRaft, so B is a follower that never campaigns; a third inmem transport connected to B sends AppendEntries(Term=1, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[index 2..L term 1]) for the defect sub-case or [index 2..L-1] for the control sub-case. Both sub-cases then connect A and B, call A.AddVoter(B, addrB, 0, 1s) without blocking on the future, sleep 300 ms, read the InstallSnapshot counter, sleep 1200 ms, read it again, and emit CA_EVENT loop_observe with the counter pair, the snapshot index, and the follower's applied and last indexes together with the leader's last and commit indexes.
experiment.responsibility: Leader-side replication must make progress for a follower that is behind rather than re-shipping the whole snapshot indefinitely, and a snapshot install must remove the follower-side condition that caused the rejection.

investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot but never calls setLastLog nor invalidates the pre-existing log entry at L. getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, so once the snapshot makes lastSnapshotIndex == L while the stale log entry keeps lastLogIndex == L, the tie is resolved in favour of the stale log term. The follower's PrevLogEntry==L check then compares the leader's snapshot term T against the stale term and answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. The leader sets nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1), which lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) then needs the leader's own log entry L-1, which is absent once the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index (compactLogsWithTrailing can leave firstIndex > L-1), so replicateTo jumps to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the same snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
investigations.discriminator: Drive one node with real RPCs: bootstrap it as a Nonvoter, seed a command at index 2 with an AppendEntries whose Term is 2, install an InstallSnapshot with LastLogIndex=2 and LastLogTerm=3, then send AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The necessary property is met only if the last append succeeds; the suspicion holds if it fails while an otherwise identical control node without the seeded entry succeeds. Refuted if the post-snapshot append succeeds in both cases, or if getLastEntry reports the snapshot term for index 2.

gaps.question: Does the leader side actually restore the blocking state in one execution: with a leader whose log has been compacted so that the snapshot index L is at its head, does an unrepairable follower produce repeated InstallSnapshot attempts with no committed progress rather than converging after one snapshot?

investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: Reconfirmed against the retained receipt: the follower keeps the log-derived term for the snapshot index and therefore rejects the leader's boundary AppendEntries; the leader-facing retry cycle remains source-sourced pending its own execution.

gaps.question: Reachability: can one compatible multi-node history legally produce the precondition (a follower holding an earlier-term entry at exactly the index where a later-term leader later commits and snapshots), rather than the harness's single seeded AppendEntries, without the follower's higher term forcing the leader to step down?

knowledge.statement: On accepting an InstallSnapshot, installSnapshot sets lastApplied=req.LastLogIndex and lastSnapshot=(req.LastLogIndex,req.LastLogTerm), restores latest and committed configuration from the snapshot payload, then clears the log store (removeOldLogs) for a monotonic store or compacts it (compactLogs(req.LastLogIndex)) otherwise, and finally sets resp.Success=true. It never calls setLastLog and never truncates a pre-existing log suffix at or above req.LastLogIndex, so lastLogIndex keeps its pre-snapshot value and a stale entry at the snapshot index can remain in the store.
knowledge.conditions: Reached only when the RPC header passes checkRPCHeader, the snapshot version is supported, req.Term >= currentTerm, the snapshot bytes are fully received (n == req.Size) and the FSM restore succeeds.

knowledge.statement: raftState.getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex,lastSnapshotIndex) and getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, otherwise (lastSnapshotIndex,lastSnapshotTerm). The comparison is on index only, so when the two sources name the same index with different terms the log-derived term wins. appendEntries uses this as the PrevLogEntry==lastIdx fast path and otherwise reads logs.GetLog(PrevLogEntry); a term mismatch or a missing entry yields Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any *Raft whose log and snapshot were written by different ingest paths (NewRaft startup restore, installSnapshot, takeSnapshot, liveBootstrap, dispatchLogs, AppendEntries append, restoreUserSnapshot).

knowledge.statement: In the executed harness, after a successful InstallSnapshot with LastLogIndex=2/LastLogTerm=3, the defect-case node (which had earlier stored a term-2 command at index 2) reported last_log_index=2, last_log_term=2, last_snapshot_index=2, last_snapshot_term=3, get_last_entry_index=2, get_last_entry_term=2, and then rejected the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3 (success=false, no_retry_backoff=true, resp_last_log=2). The otherwise identical control node, with no earlier entry at index 2, reported last_log_index=1, get_last_entry_index=2, get_last_entry_term=3 and accepted the same AppendEntries (success=true, no_retry_backoff=false).
knowledge.conditions: One process, root package '.', InmemTransport and InmemStore (non-monotonic), server-1 bootstrapped as a Nonvoter so it never campaigns, server-2 acting as the RPC producer; the two sub-cases differ only in whether an earlier-term (term 2) command was first stored at the snapshot index. Applies to the frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df. Observed in retained CheckRun 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1 (experiment c4f67dac947d44fe86d65b317d5d5b4-experiment, exit 0, tests_passed): parsed indices 5 and 6 (defect sub-case) and 1 and 2 (control sub-case).

scope.description: Two nodes in one process over InmemTransport: 'server-1' under test (Nonvoter so it never campaigns) and 'server-2' as the RPC producer. A control and a defect case run the same two/three RPC steps and differ only in whether an earlier-term leader first stored a command at the snapshot index.
assumptions: The isolated target executes the root package '.' directly; the harness is an in-package test so it may call unexported handlers and state accessors.
InmemTransport with two connected transports suffices because the claims concern one follower's response to a leader's RPCs; only the InmemStore (non-monotonic) is exercised.
BootstrapCluster writes the configuration entry that makes server-1 a Nonvoter, so the node never starts an election and the driven RPCs keep a stable term.
excluded: No net/tcp transport and no multi-node partition history; the leader-side snapshot loop is out of scope for this harness.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap server-1 as a Nonvoter in a configuration whose only Voter is server-2 (BootstrapCluster then NewRaft, so the node starts its own run/runFSM loops). Defect case step 1: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=2, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[{Index:2,Term:2,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=1) so the node stores a term-2 entry at index 2. Step 2: server-2 sends InstallSnapshot(SnapshotVersion=1, Term=3, LastLogIndex=2, LastLogTerm=3, Configuration=<server-1 Nonvoter/server-2 Voter>, ConfigurationIndex=1, Size=len(payload), payload=msgpack-encoded empty [][]byte) which the MockFSM restores. Step 3: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=3, PrevLogEntry=2, PrevLogTerm=3, Entries=[{Index:3,Term:3,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=2). The control repeats steps 2-3 only. Each step emits CA_EVENT JSON with the response and the post-snapshot last_log/last_snapshot/getLastEntry values.
basis.responsibility: installSnapshot and raftState.getLastEntry must leave a single, unchallenged view of the last durable entry: a snapshot supersedes any log entry at the same index.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader side (replication.go 223, 256, 286-300, 370): nextIndex becomes L via max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); setPreviousLog(L) requires the leader's entry L-1; once the leader has compacted past L (compactLogsWithTrailing can set firstIndex > L-1) that lookup returns ErrLogNotFound, which routes to SEND_SNAP and re-installs the same snapshot. Local construction feedback (harness assurance_generated_test.go, both sub-cases, run in a scratch copy) matched the prediction exactly: with the stale same-index entry, state_after_snapshot reported last_log_index=2/last_log_term=2 against last_snapshot_index=2/last_snapshot_term=3 and the follow-up append returned success=false/no_retry_backoff=true; without the seeded entry the same append returned success=true. That run is not a retained receipt, so the defect claim is left unresolved pending the controller's execution of the registered experiment; the leader-side loop of the gap above is likewise still unexecuted.
counterevidence: Behind-follower case does not trigger it: when the follower's lastLogIndex is below the snapshot index, getLastEntry returns the snapshot pair and the appended entries are accepted (observed as the harness control: last_log_index=1 < last_snapshot_index=2 -> success=true).

With the default TrailingLogs the leader normally retains entries below its snapshot index, so setPreviousLog(L) succeeds, the leader backs off one index and appendEntries truncates the conflicting suffix from its stored copy, converging without a snapshot loop; the loop needs the leader to have compacted up to or past L.
limitations: The retained execution has not yet run in the controller; conclusions rest on source plus non-retained local construction feedback.
The end-to-end repeated-snapshot cycle (the registered gap) was not executed; only the follower-side boundary rejection was observed, and the leader-side cycle is argued from source.

Reachability of the precondition through a full replica history was not exercised: the harness seeds the older-term entry at L with a legal AppendEntries from a term-2 leader, but a full multi-node history (old leader's uncommitted entry surviving while a new leader commits its own entry at L and compacts) is not driven.

interpretations.rationale: Source plus the retained receipt establish a violating witness, but this batch cannot link the receipt to a fixed experiment id, so the measured conclusion is reported as unresolved rather than asserted. Retained receipt: CheckRun 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1 (exit 0, outcome tests_passed) from experiment c4f67dac947d44fe86d65b317d5d5b4-experiment. Parsed indices: 5 (state_after_snapshot, defect sub-case) reports last_log_index=2, last_log_term=2, last_snapshot_index=2, last_snapshot_term=3, get_last_entry_term=2; 6 (post_snapshot_append, defect) reports success=false, no_retry_backoff=true, resp_last_log=2; 1 (control state) reports last_log_index=1, get_last_entry_term=3; 2 (control append) reports success=true. Both sub-cases installed the snapshot successfully (indices 0 and 4), so the only difference is the earlier-term entry at the snapshot index. Necessary property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L=2,T=3) the node must accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The receipt contradicts it in the defect sub-case and satisfies it in the control. Mechanism from source: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but never setLastLog nor invalidates the log entry at L; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, which is exactly the tie for a same-index earlier-term entry; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1502) then answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader-facing consequence, source-sourced and still unexecuted: nextIndex=max(min(nextIndex-1,resp.LastLog+1),1) lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) needs the leader's entry L-1; if the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index that lookup is ErrLogNotFound, so replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
counterevidence: The behind-follower case is not a defect and was observed as the control: with last_log_index=1 below last_snapshot_index=2 the node reports get_last_entry_term=3 and accepts the boundary AppendEntries (index 2, success=true).

No leader-side oscillation is established by this receipt: the run drove RPCs directly and never exercised a leader's followerReplication/nextIndex, so the loop remains a source argument with its own open gap.
limitations: Only the InmemStore (non-monotonic) path was executed; the monotonic-store branch of installSnapshot (removeOldLogs) was not run, although the same getLastEntry tie is expected to apply because lastLogIndex is likewise never reset.

The precondition was produced by a single legal AppendEntries from a term-2 producer rather than by a full multi-node history; reachability through a complete replica-set history is registered as a new gap.
The consequence for a live cluster (a follower that cannot be repaired while the leader keeps snapshotting, i.e. explicit non-progress) is argued from source and not yet executed end to end.
interpretations.joint_history: The cited receipt 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1 is the execution of the experiment registered earlier under this same investigation (@q-snapshot-boundary, experiment c4f67dac947d44fe86d65b317d5d5b4-experiment) with harness assurance_generated_test.go and the declared prefix. It runs on the same frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df and the same root package '.', so its producer history is the harness the investigation describes: BootstrapCluster(Nonvoter server-1) then NewRaft, an optional term-2 AppendEntries seeding index 2, one InstallSnapshot(2,3) and the boundary AppendEntries(PrevLogEntry=2,PrevLogTerm=3). The interpretation adds no second receipt; both state and response observations come from that single execution (parsed indices 5,6 defect and 1,2 control), which is the same witness history rather than two merged fragments.

result.summary: Attacked the registered leader-side gap with a new independently assessable investigation, @q-snapshot-loop, aimed at the replication responsibility rather than the follower ingest responsibility. Source Behavior added (@b-snapshot-loop-cycle): on a rejected AppendEntries the leader rewinds nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); when that lands on the follower's snapshot boundary L and the leader's log has been compacted so L-1 is gone, setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, sendLatestSnapshot sets nextIndex=L+1, and the next append carries PrevLogEntry=L again, restoring the preconditions of the rejection with no repair. Registered experiment update-03.json (harness assurance_generated_test.go, now the two-node loop harness in the draft): server-A bootstrapped as a single-voter leader with TrailingLogs=0 takes a user snapshot at L and compacts; server-B is a Nonvoter seeded by a legal term-1 AppendEntries up to L (defect) or L-1 (control); A then AddVoter(B) and the counter of InstallSnapshot calls plus the follower's applied index is sampled at 300 ms and 1500 ms. Local construction feedback on the same harness design: control = one InstallSnapshot, follower applied index 9; defect = install_snapshot_calls_early 2675 / late 15920 with follower applied index pinned at L=8, i.e. bounded non-progress with the retry cycle, and leader commit still advancing to 9 so the claim is scoped to that follower's replication. The interpretation is recorded as conclusion=unresolved / defect_claim omitted with the counterevidence and limitations (InmemStore only, seeded rather than full-history precondition) so the measured conclusion waits for the controller's retained receipt. Structural validation returned valid=true.

scope.description: Two nodes in one process over InmemTransport: 'server-1' under test (Nonvoter so it never campaigns) and 'server-2' as the RPC producer. A control and a defect case run the same two/three RPC steps and differ only in whether an earlier-term leader first stored a command at the snapshot index.
assumptions: The isolated target executes the root package '.' directly; the harness is an in-package test so it may call unexported handlers and state accessors.
InmemTransport with two connected transports suffices because the claims concern one follower's response to a leader's RPCs; only the InmemStore (non-monotonic) is exercised.
BootstrapCluster writes the configuration entry that makes server-1 a Nonvoter, so the node never starts an election and the driven RPCs keep a stable term.
excluded: No net/tcp transport and no multi-node partition history; the leader-side snapshot loop is out of scope for this harness.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap server-1 as a Nonvoter in a configuration whose only Voter is server-2 (BootstrapCluster then NewRaft, so the node starts its own run/runFSM loops). Defect case step 1: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=2, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[{Index:2,Term:2,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=1) so the node stores a term-2 entry at index 2. Step 2: server-2 sends InstallSnapshot(SnapshotVersion=1, Term=3, LastLogIndex=2, LastLogTerm=3, Configuration=<server-1 Nonvoter/server-2 Voter>, ConfigurationIndex=1, Size=len(payload), payload=msgpack-encoded empty [][]byte) which the MockFSM restores. Step 3: server-2 sends AppendEntries(Term=3, PrevLogEntry=2, PrevLogTerm=3, Entries=[{Index:3,Term:3,Type:LogCommand}], LeaderCommitIndex=2). The control repeats steps 2-3 only. Each step emits CA_EVENT JSON with the response and the post-snapshot last_log/last_snapshot/getLastEntry values.
basis.responsibility: installSnapshot and raftState.getLastEntry must leave a single, unchallenged view of the last durable entry: a snapshot supersedes any log entry at the same index.

scope.description: One process, two real Raft instances over InmemTransport. server-A is bootstrapped as a single-voter cluster, becomes leader, applies six commands, then takes a user snapshot with TrailingLogs=0 so its retained log starts above the snapshot index. server-B is bootstrapped as a Nonvoter under the same configuration so it never campaigns, and is seeded with earlier-term (term 1) commands up to the snapshot index (defect) or one index short of it (control) via a legal AppendEntries from a third in-memory transport. server-A and server-B are then connected and server-A is asked to AddVoter(server-B).
assumptions: The isolated target runs the root package '.' directly, so the harness is an in-package test and may wrap the transport to count InstallSnapshot calls.
A single-voter cluster bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster reaches leadership on its own after the election timeout, which keeps the leader-side prefix free of partition machinery.
AddVoter is issued without waiting on its future because the config entry cannot commit while the peer is unrepairable; the observation window starts after a fixed delay.
excluded: No network transport, no partitions, and no more than one peer; leader elections among multiple voters are out of scope.
The follower-side boundary rejection is already covered by the earlier experiment and is not re-derived here.

basis.prefix: server-A: inmem transport wrapped by a counting decorator that increments on every InstallSnapshot call; BootstrapCluster(conf.TrailingLogs=0, config={A:Voter}); NewRaft; wait for Leader; six Apply(new command) calls; Snapshot() and record its Index L and the store's FirstIndex. server-B: separate inmem transport, BootstrapCluster(config={A:Voter,B:Nonvoter}) then NewRaft, so B is a follower that never campaigns; a third inmem transport connected to B sends AppendEntries(Term=1, PrevLogEntry=1, PrevLogTerm=1, Entries=[index 2..L term 1]) for the defect sub-case or [index 2..L-1] for the control sub-case. Both sub-cases then connect A and B, call A.AddVoter(B, addrB, 0, 1s) without blocking on the future, sleep 300 ms, read the InstallSnapshot counter, sleep 1200 ms, read it again, and emit CA_EVENT loop_observe with the counter pair, the snapshot index, and the follower's applied and last indexes together with the leader's last and commit indexes.
basis.responsibility: Leader-side replication must make progress for a follower that is behind rather than re-shipping the whole snapshot indefinitely, and a snapshot install must remove the follower-side condition that caused the rejection.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader side (replication.go 223, 256, 286-300, 370): nextIndex becomes L via max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); setPreviousLog(L) requires the leader's entry L-1; once the leader has compacted past L (compactLogsWithTrailing can set firstIndex > L-1) that lookup returns ErrLogNotFound, which routes to SEND_SNAP and re-installs the same snapshot. Local construction feedback (harness assurance_generated_test.go, both sub-cases, run in a scratch copy) matched the prediction exactly: with the stale same-index entry, state_after_snapshot reported last_log_index=2/last_log_term=2 against last_snapshot_index=2/last_snapshot_term=3 and the follow-up append returned success=false/no_retry_backoff=true; without the seeded entry the same append returned success=true. That run is not a retained receipt, so the defect claim is left unresolved pending the controller's execution of the registered experiment; the leader-side loop of the gap above is likewise still unexecuted.
counterevidence: Behind-follower case does not trigger it: when the follower's lastLogIndex is below the snapshot index, getLastEntry returns the snapshot pair and the appended entries are accepted (observed as the harness control: last_log_index=1 < last_snapshot_index=2 -> success=true).

With the default TrailingLogs the leader normally retains entries below its snapshot index, so setPreviousLog(L) succeeds, the leader backs off one index and appendEntries truncates the conflicting suffix from its stored copy, converging without a snapshot loop; the loop needs the leader to have compacted up to or past L.
limitations: The retained execution has not yet run in the controller; conclusions rest on source plus non-retained local construction feedback.
The end-to-end repeated-snapshot cycle (the registered gap) was not executed; only the follower-side boundary rejection was observed, and the leader-side cycle is argued from source.

Reachability of the precondition through a full replica history was not exercised: the harness seeds the older-term entry at L with a legal AppendEntries from a term-2 leader, but a full multi-node history (old leader's uncommitted entry surviving while a new leader commits its own entry at L and compacts) is not driven.

interpretations.rationale: Source plus the retained receipt establish a violating witness, but this batch cannot link the receipt to a fixed experiment id, so the measured conclusion is reported as unresolved rather than asserted. Retained receipt: CheckRun 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1 (exit 0, outcome tests_passed) from experiment c4f67dac947d44fe86d65b317d5d5b4-experiment. Parsed indices: 5 (state_after_snapshot, defect sub-case) reports last_log_index=2, last_log_term=2, last_snapshot_index=2, last_snapshot_term=3, get_last_entry_term=2; 6 (post_snapshot_append, defect) reports success=false, no_retry_backoff=true, resp_last_log=2; 1 (control state) reports last_log_index=1, get_last_entry_term=3; 2 (control append) reports success=true. Both sub-cases installed the snapshot successfully (indices 0 and 4), so the only difference is the earlier-term entry at the snapshot index. Necessary property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L=2,T=3) the node must accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The receipt contradicts it in the defect sub-case and satisfies it in the control. Mechanism from source: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but never setLastLog nor invalidates the log entry at L; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, which is exactly the tie for a same-index earlier-term entry; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1502) then answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader-facing consequence, source-sourced and still unexecuted: nextIndex=max(min(nextIndex-1,resp.LastLog+1),1) lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) needs the leader's entry L-1; if the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index that lookup is ErrLogNotFound, so replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
counterevidence: The behind-follower case is not a defect and was observed as the control: with last_log_index=1 below last_snapshot_index=2 the node reports get_last_entry_term=3 and accepts the boundary AppendEntries (index 2, success=true).

No leader-side oscillation is established by this receipt: the run drove RPCs directly and never exercised a leader's followerReplication/nextIndex, so the loop remains a source argument with its own open gap.
limitations: Only the InmemStore (non-monotonic) path was executed; the monotonic-store branch of installSnapshot (removeOldLogs) was not run, although the same getLastEntry tie is expected to apply because lastLogIndex is likewise never reset.

The precondition was produced by a single legal AppendEntries from a term-2 producer rather than by a full multi-node history; reachability through a complete replica-set history is registered as a new gap.
The consequence for a live cluster (a follower that cannot be repaired while the leader keeps snapshotting, i.e. explicit non-progress) is argued from source and not yet executed end to end.
interpretations.joint_history: The cited receipt 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1 is the execution of the experiment registered earlier under this same investigation (@q-snapshot-boundary, experiment c4f67dac947d44fe86d65b317d5d5b4-experiment) with harness assurance_generated_test.go and the declared prefix. It runs on the same frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df and the same root package '.', so its producer history is the harness the investigation describes: BootstrapCluster(Nonvoter server-1) then NewRaft, an optional term-2 AppendEntries seeding index 2, one InstallSnapshot(2,3) and the boundary AppendEntries(PrevLogEntry=2,PrevLogTerm=3). The interpretation adds no second receipt; both state and response observations come from that single execution (parsed indices 5,6 defect and 1,2 control), which is the same witness history rather than two merged fragments.

interpretations.rationale: Source identifies the exact cycle, but the measured end-to-end result is deliberately left unresolved until the controller retains an execution of this experiment. Local construction feedback on the same harness design showed install_snapshot_calls_early=1/late=1 with follower_applied_index=9 for the control peer, versus install_snapshot_calls_early=2675/late=15920 with follower_applied_index=8 pinned at the snapshot index for the peer holding an earlier-term entry at that index; that local run is not a retained receipt and is recorded here only as construction feedback. The cycle's weakest necessary link is the leader-side ErrLogNotFound branch, which depends on the log store reporting ErrLogNotFound for L-1 after compaction; the harness uses InmemStore, whose DeleteRange resets to empty once everything is deleted, and the leader's first retained index in that run was 9 with the snapshot at 8.
counterevidence: The control peer converged in one snapshot, so the repeated-snapshot behaviour is not a property of adding a voter alone.
In the same run the leader's own commit index still advanced to 9, so the no-progress claim is scoped to that follower's replication and applied index, not to the leader's commit index.
limitations: Source-only conclusion: the receipt for this experiment has not been produced yet.
Only InmemTransport/InmemStore were used; a monotonic LogStore clears all logs on snapshot install, which changes the store-level path but not the follower's stale last-entry term.
The peer's earlier-term entry was seeded by a legal AppendEntries from a term-1 producer rather than by a complete replica-set history; that reachability question stays open.
